problem: End-to-end DRL object-goal navigation generalizes poorly to unseen scenes and especially unseen target classes; prior relation-learning methods rely on fixed prior knowledge graphs, fixed-size detection matrices tied to predefined classes, or heavy transformers.
motivation: Real household environments have varying object placements and novel target classes, so a policy needs domain-independent visual representations. The paper observes that focusing on the observed objects most related to the target, and encoding the difference between current and desired states rather than class-specific features, should transfer to unseen classes.
key_idea: A target attention module selects detected objects (bbox plus GloVe embedding) most correlated with the target, and a Siamese architecture encodes the absolute difference between the current and target states as a class-independent representation for an A3C policy.
insight: The ablations show TA and SA are complementary: in the zero-shot 18/4 split, unseen-class SR is 8.1 with neither module, 17.0 with SA only, 14.2 with TA only, and 62.5 with both, so the gain is mainly from their combination. On seen objects, TA contributes more (SR 50.0 to 76.3 with TA alone vs 58.9 with SA alone). Attending to target-relevant objects before differencing against the target state yields class-independent features, and without TA the SA-only network is distracted by unrelated objects.
method: Input: per-object vector [x, y, area, 300-d GloVe] from ground-truth boxes in AI2-THOR (YOLOv7 in the real world), stacked into an n×303 matrix with variable n; the target vector is [0.5, 0.5, 0.25, GloVe(target)].

Target Attention (TA): a shared linear layer maps target and objects, their dot product gives the correspondence vector V_corr, a softmax gives attention V_att, and V_att multiplies the Linear1 features to give a weighted feature focused on target-related objects.

Siamese Architecture (SA): two weight-sharing linear branches encode the TA-selected object feature and the target vector, then take the absolute difference with dropout to obtain the class-independent representation.
Policy: the representation goes through a feed-forward layer and an LSTM into an A3C actor-critic, trained end-to-end for 6M episodes.
Reward: -0.01 per step, R_t=5 on Done with the target visible, plus a partial reward R_p = R_t·Pr(t|p)·k (k=0.1) for seeing a parent object (from MJOLNIR), given once per parent object.
Zero-shot protocol: detections of unseen classes are removed during training, so the network learns nothing about them.

setting.backbone: TDANet (TA + Siamese + LSTM + A3C, trained from scratch); GloVe embeddings; YOLOv7 (COCO-pretrained) as the detector for the real robot
setting.training_data: AI2-THOR v1.0.1 offline data, 20 training rooms per room type (80 rooms), 22 target classes, 6M episodes; no extra data
setting.observation: monocular RGB, converted to detected bounding boxes plus word embeddings (GT boxes in simulation)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead 0.25m, RotateLeft/Right 45°, LookUp/Down 30°, Done
setting.privileged: ground-truth object bounding boxes in AI2-THOR (YOLOv7 detections in the real world)

The ablation table for seen objects prints 78.8/30.6 and 67.7/33.4 for the full model, slightly different from Table 1.
results: TDANet reaches SR 78.2 / SPL 30.6 (L>=1) on seen objects in unseen AI2-THOR scenes, beating Li et al. (71.0 / 19.6) and SSNet (63.7 / 22.8). In zero-shot unseen-class navigation (18/4 split) it gets SR 62.5 / SPL 25.3 vs SSNet 28.6 / 9.0. It was also deployed on a TurtleBot4 with YOLOv7 and reached an unseen object (Book), shown as a qualitative trajectory only.
limitations: Uses ground-truth bounding boxes in simulation and relies on an object detector in the real world; the real-world evaluation is a single qualitative trajectory, not quantitative.
Evaluated only in AI2-THOR single-room scenes with 22 classes; collision avoidance and complex environments are left for future work.
Reward still uses a parent-object prior (R_p) inherited from MJOLNIR.
